title: Dashboard Panel Class
prompt: A React dashboard panel receives selected and disabled props. Write a helper that returns "panel", adds " selected" when selected is true, and adds " disabled" when disabled is true.

explanation.beginner:
Example: dashboardPanelClass({}) produces "panel". Map each explicitly supported state to its exact output text or value. Separate state selection from formatting.

Compare “adds selected and disabled classes”: input [{"selected":true,"disabled":true}] produces "panel selected disabled". Explain which rule causes the difference before writing code.
explanation.junior:
Map each explicitly supported state to its exact output text or value. Separate state selection from formatting.

Tempting mistake: Capitalization, whitespace, and boolean-versus-string output are part of the contract; truthiness alone may combine distinct states.

Trace the branch conditions and any accumulator or lookup after each input. Keep the return contract separate from how it is calculated.

Regression check: preserve the contract illustrated by “adds selected and disabled classes”, then change one boundary in a new test. The solution below is one implementation; another is valid when it preserves the same behavior.
